items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: Perez and the Basie band, Buster Bailey and all of them had started experimenting

ctx.x: They -- now, Perez and the Basie band, Buster Bailey and all of them had started experimenting with what we called in Kansas City, 'running out of a key.' Now, that meant that the rhythm section stayed straight. They didn't go dropping those bombs or anything.

It was the horns that was going on. They were playing the flatted fifths and all that, stuff scales. But the rhythm section played straight, just like the Basie rhythm section or our rhythm section plays, you know. But then we came, got to New York and run across this new thing, you know, that Max and them developed, and that's really how I managed to stick in there as long as I did with all of them, Monk and Diz and all of them, because now they needed a heavy bass player, strong player to carry the beat while…
